points.description: States the purpose: both are broadcast methods that reduce duplicate packets compared with flooding. Explains RPF: a node X receiving a packet from sender S via neighbor N checks its unicast routing table and forwards it to all adjacent nodes except N only if it would send packets to S via N (i.e. packet arrived on the best route). Explains RPB: same as RPF, but nodes learn from unicast traffic which spanning trees/best paths they belong to, and forward only on edges that are part of a spanning tree (excluding the incoming link). Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.5 if the purpose and RPF mechanism are correct but RPB is missing or wrong (or vice versa for a correct RPB with RPF missing).
